item.description: Today, the members of the nine federally recognized tribes in Oregon carry forward a deep knowledge of this place and traditions that have endured and evolved for thousands of years.

item.title: Oregon - Wikipedia
item.description: The Oregon Treaty of 1846 formally brought Oregon under American sovereignty, and the Oregon Territory was created two years later. Oregon was admitted to the United States on February 14, 1859, becoming the 33rd state.

item.title: Travel Oregon | Oregon Vacations & Travel Guide
item.description: Oregon is on the West Coast, right between Washington and California. Made up of seven diverse regions, Oregon has the ocean, mountains, valleys, high desert, cities, small towns, and almost everything in between.

item.title: Oregon Maps & Facts - World Atlas
item.description: Oregon, also nicknamed, “The Beaver State”, is located in the Pacific Northwest United States. It shares its northern border with Washington, its eastern border with Idaho, its southern border with Nevada and California, and its western coastline with the Pacific Ocean.

item.title: Visit Oregon | Oregon Travel & Vacation Guide
item.description: The Oregon Travel Guide gives you the overview — 8 regions, top attractions, honest recommendations, and the practical details you’ll actually need. Then, The Oregon Insider lands in your inbox weekly with seasonal tips, new itineraries, and the kind of specific, opinionated recommendations you won’t find in any official tourism brochure.

item.title: Oregon | Geography, History, Capital, Map, Population, & Facts | Britannica
item.description: Oregon, constituent state of the U.S. It is bounded to the north by Washington, to the east by Idaho, to the south by Nevada and California, and to the west by the Pacific Ocean. Its largest city is Portland and its capital is Salem, both of which are in the northwestern part of the state.

item.description: Coastal towns, wine country, mountain trails – there is no shortage of things to do in Oregon. Find out where to start on this list of the best places to visit in Oregon.

item.title: The 21 Top Things to Do in Oregon - U.S. News Travel
item.description: From vineyards to geological sites, the Beaver State offers a variety of attractions to explore. Visit beaches, forests, mountains and cities across Oregon.

item.title: Geography of Oregon - Wikipedia
item.description: Oregon's population is largely concentrated in the Willamette Valley, which stretches from Eugene in the south (home of the University of Oregon) through Corvallis (home of Oregon State University) and Salem (the capital) to Portland (Oregon's largest city).
